extracted.intended_audience: press officers, institutional communications staff, science journalists, and researchers preparing embargoed press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and distributing press releases that are subject to a news embargo (including coordination with journal/publisher embargo policies such as the Ingelfinger rule). Covers formatting, timing, distribution, and consequences of breaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly identify embargoed press releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases must be clearly identified as embargoed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use conventional prominent labeling (e.g., put 'EMBARGOED UNTIL [DATE/TIME]' at the top of the release) so recipients immediately know the content is under embargo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include precise embargo date, time, and time zone
rubrics_metrics.description: Must include the embargo date and time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a precise example (e.g., 'Embargoed until 11:00 a.m. ET, Monday, March 15, 2026') and always specify the time zone to avoid confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press officers responsible for third-party compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Press officers are responsible for ensuring third parties honor the embargo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take steps to inform and contractually or procedurally require partners, vendors, and collaborators to respect the embargo; failure of third parties to comply is the sender's responsibility to manage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use conventional embargo formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Conventional formats: 'EMBARGOED UNTIL [DATE/TIME]' at top of release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow common conventions so newsroom systems and journalists recognize embargoed material; consistent formatting reduces accidental early publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate timing with journal or publisher embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate timing with the journal/publisher embargo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align the press release embargo with the journal's embargo schedule since many journals treat the embargo time as the official publication time; verify publisher rules before distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat embargo time as the official publication time
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not allow public disclosure before this time; consider this the moment when information becomes public for purposes of media relations and journal policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use embargoed advance distribution services when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases sent to EurekAlert/Newswise typically go out under embargo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When working with scientific publishers or research institutions, use established embargoed distribution channels (EurekAlert, Newswise) that are designed to handle embargoed materials and advance copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Send releases 2–7 days before embargo lift
rubrics_metrics.description: Send releases 2-7 days before embargo lift.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide lead time in this window so journalists can prepare accurate stories while the embargo is in effect; exact timing may depend on complexity and verification needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide journalists adequate lead time to verify and obtain quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide journalists enough lead time to verify, get expert quotes, and write.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure supporting materials and experts are available in advance so reporters can check facts, interview sources, and prepare copy that will publish promptly when the embargo lifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify all associated media materials as embargoed
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify all media materials (figures, supplementary materials) clearly as embargoed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label figures, supplementary files, data sets, and other assets with embargo markings and include them in the embargoed distribution to avoid inadvertent early sharing of supporting materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to journal policies such as the Ingelfinger rule (avoid prior disclosure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many journals use variants of the Ingelfinger rule to restrain scientists from disclosing research to journalists prior to publication; original principle: 'articles are accepted for consideration with the understanding that they are contributed for publication solely in this journal.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand publisher restrictions: premature public disclosure may jeopardize journal consideration. Use embargoed advance copies when journals permit advance coverage under embargo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of violating an embargo
rubrics_metrics.description: Violating embargo can result in being cut off from advance copies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of enforcement: outlets and publishers may refuse future embargoed access or take other sanctions if embargoes are breached; weigh risks when sharing information.
